recipes.name: Slow Cooker Pozole
ingredients_raw: 1 (2 pound) boneless pork loin roast, cut into 1-inch cubes
0.5 teaspoon cayenne pepper, or to taste

steps.text: Heat oil in a skillet over high heat. Add pork; cook and stir just until meat is browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Place meat in a 4-quart slow cooker. Pour enchilada sauce over the meat. Top with hominy, onion, chilies, garlic, cayenne pepper, and oregano. Pour in enough water to fill the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on High for 6 to 7 hours. Stir in cilantro and salt. Cook on Low for 30 minutes more.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Pozole
raw_recipe.description: This pozole recipe is made in a slow cooker with pork, hominy, green chiles, and enchilada sauce for an easy version of the classic Mexican soup.

review.reviewBody: I never thought about making pozole in the crockpot until I came across this recipe! It's just as yummy cooked this way. The only change was that I added some pieces of chicken to the soup - that is how we've always made our pozole, a mix of pork/chicken. And I add a bit more fresh diced garlic since we love it. We serve our soup in a big bowl, add a scoop of refried beans( it thickens the soup) and add condiments - chopped onion/green onion/chopped cilantro/a pinch of oregano/a twist of some lemon or lime slices to taste. Delicious, filling, comfort food. Serve all year - not just for New Year!

To sum things up, I'm a white girl and my husband is Mexican. He's used to his mom's pozole, so I was nervous about making this. To my surprise, he loved it! Even called is family to say how good I can make pozole. Next time I may leave out the onions. It added to the flavor, but the onion slices aren't traditional and threw us off a bit. I also made this a little more simpler by eliminating the step of cubing the meat. I added a whole pork loin. It falls about eventually, so I didn't see the need for cutting it. I also added more hominy and a packet of Goya Sazon seasoning (that stuff is great in/on almost everything, it's a secret ingredient I use often).

This is a flavor bomb. My first try at posole, and yet I was compelled to alter the recipe in this way - I browned the pork chunks (I think I used about 4 lbs.) in a cast iron skillet (after a healthy seasoning of salt, pepper and olive oil), put that in the slow cooker and then added the sliced onion to the skillet to pull off all the delicious pork drippings from the browned bottom, tossed in the garlic (double the garlic - used 3 tablespoons minced) and 2 very big, diced poblano peppers and half a diced green pepper, and also added 1-2 tablespoon of chili powder and a tablespoon of dried achiote chili, sautéed that for 5-10 mins and then added a can of Rotel (to my taste, after tasting it, feeling it needed a bit more tomato flavor). I used both green enchilada and red enchilada sauce (add that to the onions and peppers in the skillet and let it cook together for a bit, salting to taste). Poured that over the pork and let it go for 6 hours. Buddy it was a home run!!! In the rotation fo'-eva!

Thanks so much for this recipe! It satisfied the craving I've had for posole after moving away from New Mexico where I could get great posole and Hatch green chile everywhere. Complicated recipes and a lack of dried chiles where I am at now in the Midwest always kept me from trying to make it, but this recipe is so easy and tastes just as good by using enchilada sauce instead that I wished I had made this earlier. I browned the meat in the Instant Pot and pressure cooked everything for 30 minutes with a natural release for about 20 minutes. I used 3 packets of Frontera green enchilada sauce and a can of Ortega diced green chiles.

Super in love with a quick easy recipe! I used my pressure pot Ninja Foodi and I only had to cook it for an hour. My husband likes it spicy so I added ground up jalapeño, serrano, and habenero to it. I read thru a lot of recipes and comments that all said authentic posole had a mix of pork and chicken so I made sure to make it like that. I substituted chicken broth. I like to eat it with fresh avocado, cabbage and lime! Tasty and quick! My friends fell in love with it as well! ??!

This is excellent, not traditional- but delicious! I used one 28 oz can of Las Palmas medium green chile enchilada sauce, one 15 oz can of Hatch red enchilada sauce, one 27 oz can of Hatch chopped green chilies, and a 3-4 lb pork roast (cut into 4 chunks and browned in a skillet before putting in the crockpot- also sauteed the onions and garlic before putting in the crockpot), and one can Juanita's Foods 25 oz can of hominy for the initial heating/serving, then added more broth and hominy after reheating a couple of bowls to keep it fresh and not allowing the hominy to absorb all the broth I started with. I also added one 10 oz can of the Rotel chilies and tomatoes and served with avocado slices, radishes, cilantro, and lime wedges along with a small can of the spicy diced green chilies in case anyone wanted a little extra spice, but the heat level was perfect! Enough to wake you up and warm your insides without making your eyes water. Fantastic dish.

This was a very good, very easy recipe. I increased the enchilada sauce and beef broth (instead of water) to roughly 40 ounces each, used 3 cans of hominy, and chopped versus sliced the onion. Cut the pork roast into 4 pieces and browned it and the onion/garlic before adding to the crock pot. I felt the original recipe ended up with WAY too much meat for the other ingredients. Added the hominy toward the end of the cooking time. Will make again and again!

I love this recipe my husband loves when I make Posole he's Mexican and says my posole taste as good as his mother's I made a few substitutions and additions that a few of my Latino mom friends suggested and it was perfect 1st instead of water I used a carton of chicken stock I replaced the cayenne pepper with 1 tsp Cumin and instead of pork loin I used 1lb of pork short rib & 1.5 lbs of pork neck for added flavor and seared them in butter instead of oil to seal in flavor. I also added 1 pckt of the Sazon Goya con culantro y achiote season to the slow cooker. I love this recipe and hope you post more authentic Latin recipes soon

WOW! What a delicious meal this made! I cooked it on the stove top about 3 hours on low and reduced the enchilada sauce to one can and used 4 fresh tomatoes chopped instead. The flavors were a lot more complex than I imagined they would be. I fried up some corn tortilla strips (about 1/2 inch by 2 inches) and topped the soup with them as well as an avocado slice and some crumbled queso fresco (Mexican white cheese). Chopped onions, fresh cilantro, shredded cabbage and chopped jalepenos can be used on top to garnish)

I used two cans of Mexican hominy 25oz and where it says tsp for spices I did tbsp. I used hot diced chilis and 1 1/2 tbsp minced garlic and added salt to taste. I'd dice the onion next time instead of slice.

Very good and easy. I blended many comments. Used only 2 cans of hominy and added 1 can of refried beans and 1 of pinto beans. Also used 2 chicken breasts at 1 1/2 lbs, added them whole and shredded them half way through with the hominy. Used 1 can green and 2 cans red enchilada sauce. Lime is key.
Made as per recipe. My wife can't take spicy food. So next time I eill lessen the cayenne pepper. I thoujght is was great!
Easy to make and very tasty!!
Family couldn’t quit raving about it, we will definitely be making it again! Everyone had seconds!!

Used this recipe more for reference to use the crockpot. I’m Mexican so I stuck to the traditional recipe, which does not include cilantro, green chiles, or cayenne pepper. I am curious to try making it with the canned enchilada sauce…just to see if my husband and sons will notice any difference.

I followed everyone’s advice and tweaked it!! I waited till right before serving before adding the hominy!! I also swapped enchilada sauce for Los Palmas Red Chile sauce instead …(as for the chilies, cayenne pepper, and oregano ..Left it out!!) I did a tsp of cumin and a TBL of chile powder instead…..and it turned out good!!
Really no need to brown the pork. The crock pot will make it very tender.

This was so easy to make and full of flavor! Tasted better the 2nd day. I left out the cayenne pepper since my kids were eating it. We enjoyed this as our Christmas Eve dinner and will definitely make it again!

I've made it a couple times a year for the past four years and my family loves it. Like others, I add a bit more homey and sub chili powder for cayenne. Serve with all the sides mentioned and flour tortillas heated over a gas stove grate.
This is a super easy recipe. I swapped chili powder for the Cayenne and oregano. It worked great. Also secured with cabbage.
